title: A fitted 0.12-day secondary spin gives periapse circulation for TYC 9179-1083-1 in a 4,000-year conservative test
abstract: We fit conservative inner-binary forces and the orbit together for TYC 9179-1083-1. The inputs are 153 published eclipse times, eight published velocities and eight adopted shape constraints. With aligned prescribed spins, apsidal constants 0.01 and 0.10 and one bright-tertiary radius model, a 0.12-day secondary spin gives weighted loss 144.408, mutual angle 53.222 degrees and masses 0.658, 0.540 and 1.102 solar masses. A free rotational rate gives loss 138.848 and 0.0437 +/- 0.0382 degree per year on a local linear scale. The no-rotation fit with relativity and tides gives loss 140.141 and angle 50.727 degrees. Direct three-body integration of the fitted fast-spin state gives periapse circulation over 4,000 years and eccentricity 0.0584-0.5705. The fitted free-rate state gives libration. This supplies a fitted alternative to an earlier fixed-state spin experiment. It does not detect rotation or establish equal model probability. No new observations are used. Shape weights, fixed radius ratios and stellar constants, prescribed aligned spins, sparse velocities and one local prograde branch limit the result. Code, exact source-member hashes, fitted states, direct and averaged model tracks, numerical checks and timing predictions support inspection and reproduction without bundled external records.
